feature.title: Rhythm tracker plan D11
feature.request:
Feature: Rhythm tracker plan (the work deferred under D11)

Context. AudioVisualizer's rhythm tracker (app/features/rhythm/: tempo estimation in tempo.ts, beat grid in beatTracker.ts, the orchestration in rhythmAnalyzer.ts, song changes in boundary.ts, meter in meter.ts, constants in rhythmConfig.ts) feeds every visualizer through the audio hub. The hub plans (audio-engine-alignment, hub-regressions, hub-followups) are finished. Every remaining scorecard failure belongs to the tracker. On 2026-11-22, Trevor decided this work is its own plan, made in a fresh double-diamond session ("Review decisions" in docs/agents/hub-scorecard.md). Plan it on main after PR #126 (the follow-up drain) merges.

Failing offline cells (npm run scorecard, targets v9):

| Cell | Track | Value | Target |
| beat.errorMedianMs | summer2000 | 153 ms | 40 |
| beat.errorMedianMs | low-bpm-rnb | 183 ms | 40 |
| beat.errorMedianMs, tempo.maxErrorAfterLock | 6-8-time | never locks | 40 ms, 0.020 |
| tempo.falseSongChanges | 6-8-time | 1 | 0 |
| tempo.beatlessNeverLocks | beatless | locks (1) | 0 |
| ac9.dottedChangeCounted | dotted 100→150 scenario | 0 | 1 |
| onset.f50.kick / .bass | bassline-kick-120 | 0.81 / 0.77 | 0.90 |
| gate.secondsAfterLock | half-time-shuffle, lonley, summer2000, low-bpm-rnb | 7.2, 10.8, 6.1, never | 4 s |

Also deferred: AC7 (dance-clip consistency across plays) on syncopation-no-kick, 6-8-time, high-bpm-dnb, low-bpm-rnb and syncopationbass; and syncopation-no-kick's first lock (AC5 of the audio-alignment plan). Known weaknesses with no packet yet: a 3/4 click at 180 BPM reads as 90, high-bpm-dnb first locks at 115, and the grid moves abruptly when it re-aligns.

Diagnosed causes so far.
- summer2000 (hub-scorecard.md, "Why the tracker's beat misses summer2000"): the tempo is right (127.66 bpm, ratio 1.001), but the grid locks about half a beat off the taps from 8 s to 18.5 s, then drifts toward them without settling. The kicks are on the taps. The cause is the first phase: an onset corrects a beat only within BEAT_WINDOW_FRACTION (0.2 beat, about 94 ms here), and the phase is searched again only after BEAT_LOST_BEATS (8) beats with no onset, which this track's dense onsets never allow. No single constant fixes it (ablation table in that section). The candidates are different phase evidence (weigh the kick band), keeping several phase guesses, or a re-search that doesn't wait for the onsets to stop.
- low-bpm-rnb: needs a beat tracker that keeps several phase hypotheses (see "Causes" in hub-scorecard.md). This is probably the same design as summer2000.
- half-time-shuffle's gate: the tracker counts the shuffle's 169 bpm subdivision, not its 83 bpm beat. Fixing it needs either the right beat level or a gate that searches bar lengths. Both are redesigns.
- beatless: needs a model of whether a beat is present at all.
- The dotted 100→150 change (3/2): never followed within 30 s, while 4/3 and octave changes are. One attempt was shelved; see "3/2 tempo changes: shelved" in docs/agents/audio-alignment-findings.md.
- Follow-ups moved into this plan:
  - FU-S6-three-halves-change: the shelved 3/2 attempt itself.
  - FU-boundary-dotted: BoundaryDetector can swallow a sustained dotted change forever.
  - FU-dotted-leaky: a leaky challenger counter for weak dotted rivals. It was tried and only works together with a working 3/2 rule.
  - FU-polyrhythm-grid-spec: pin the tracker on a 3:2 polyrhythm grid before any 3/2 or bar-evidence change.

  Their full packets are in the verified-diamond followups.json, marked "ejected to the D11 tracker plan".

Constraints.
- Every tracker change affects every visualizer and track. Judge it on the full npm run scorecard plus npm run scorecard:check (blocking cells that pass must not get worse), plus sweep:gate false opens.
- Some specs use it.fails to record known tracker weaknesses. Fixing one makes its spec fail until .fails is removed.
- The committed tapped truth (.debug-in/*.beats.json) is checked by hash and can't be recreated. The audio itself is local and never committed.
- The bundle is at 338.04 of 338.5 kB total JS, so a bigger tracker needs a budget decision.
- Live cells need npm run scorecard:live from the main checkout, which takes about 45 s per run. Machine load has skewed results before.
- Repo rules are in AGENTS.md: logic outside React, no allocation per frame, named exports.

Tools already available: eval:rhythm --alignment, ablate:rhythm --set, sweep:onsets, probe:rhythm, ground-truth, scorecard, scorecard:check, scorecard:live, sweep:gate, replay:gate. To get the per-beat error over time (which ablate:rhythm doesn't print), use detectFromPcm with loadWithOverrides (scripts/rhythm-tools/ablatePlugin.ts). The summer2000 diagnosis did this from a scratch script.

Open questions for the plan.
1. Is one beat-tracker redesign (several phase hypotheses, or different phase evidence) the shared fix for summer2000, low-bpm-rnb, half-time-shuffle and 6-8-time? Or are these separate problems?
2. Does the 3/2 change belong in this plan, or in a separate tempo-change plan?
3. Is a beat-presence model (beatless) in scope?
4. Which cells are required and which are stretch? Trevor's 2026-11-22 review accepted some cells as measured.
5. What is the budget for added code and CPU in the worklet?

problem.statement: The beat tracker gets the tempo right on summer2000 and low-bpm-rnb but sits off the beat, for two different reasons. On summer2000 (153 ms median beat error, target 40) the first alignment settles about half a beat off. The existing phase check never moves the grid back: it is BeatTracker's decayed 16-bin histogram of the unweighted onset sum, which needs PHASE_SHIFT_RATIO 1.15 for PHASE_SHIFT_BEATS 4. Why it stays silent there is not yet measured. On low-bpm-rnb (183 ms) the phase check does move the grid onto the beat at 16 s. The per-beat correction then pulls each beat onto a kick a sixteenth early, the period shrinks, and the grid slides back within 5 s. The phase check cannot see that slide, because its evidence turns with the grid. Visualizers that read the beat place are off, and the dancer's bass gate opens late (6.1 s, and never on low-bpm-rnb, target 4 s). Nearby failures (6-8-time, half-time-shuffle, beatless, the 3/2 dotted change, bassline-kick-120 onsets) are separate problems handled as stretch.

Band weights, the phase ratio and minimum shift, the window, a distance-weighted peak and gains were all tried, and none moved it

decisions.question: Does a phase move bump gridEpoch?
decisions.answer: No. A phase move keeps the beat numbering and counts in phaseShiftCount, as checkPhase does today. Only a numbering break bumps the epoch

options.summary: Keep the single-hypothesis PLL but add a decayed, kick-weighted phase histogram folded on the current period, and re-run the existing phase search every few beats against it (not only after 8 onset-free beats), with hysteresis.
approach: In BeatTracker add a fixed Float32Array phase histogram (about 24 bins per beat), allocated once. Each push folds the frame onset into bin (t mod period) with exponential decay (about 8 s half-life). The folded energy uses a kick-weighted onset (low band times KICK_PHASE_WEIGHT plus the other bands) passed alongside the existing sum.
On period change or changeOctave, rescale or clear the histogram (clear is simplest, since the bin index depends on the period).
Every BEAT_RESEARCH_BEATS (4) declared beats, find the histogram peak (circular smoothing over 3 bins) and compare it with the bin under the current grid phase.

If the peak is more than BEAT_WINDOW_FRACTION away and its energy is at least PHASE_RIVAL_RATIO (about 1.5) times the current bin for 2 consecutive checks, jump the grid: set the next pending beat to the peak phase, increment gridEpoch, keep beatCount monotonic and keep lastBeatTime unchanged until the next declared beat.
Otherwise do nothing, so the normal 0.4 gain PLL correction stays as is and tracks that already lock well are untouched.
Add constants to rhythmConfig.ts. Measure with ablate:rhythm, per-beat error from detectFromPcm, scorecard, scorecard:check and sweep:gate. Tune only the new constants.
Stretch slices stay separate: 3:2 grid spec (AC6), then beatless presence from histogram peak sharpness (AC7), then the 3/2 change (AC8). Update the findings docs (AC9).

pros: Smallest diff: about 80 lines, one file plus a few constants, well under the 3 kB JS budget
Per-frame cost is one bin add and one decay multiply; per-beat work is a 24-bin scan, so CPU is far below 1.25x
Re-search does not wait for onsets to stop, which is the diagnosed cause on summer2000
Hysteresis protects tracks that already lock
cons: A single hypothesis with a periodic jump still has one visible grid jump per recovery (the known abrupt re-align weakness)
Kick weighting may not fix low-bpm-rnb if the syncopated kick itself is the strongest bin; that track may need a rival-hypothesis score, which this option does not provide
Histogram on a drifting period smears; clearing on period change delays recovery
risks: Wrong jumps on swung or syncopated tracks raise false grid moves and sweep:gate false opens
New constants overfit to two tracks; ablation on the full scorecard is mandatory
Changing the grid under the dancer's gate alters first-lock and gate timings on passing tracks

options.summary: Add a preallocated phase-evidence bank to BeatTracker: a kick-weighted, leaky phase histogram over the beat period whose top few peaks are scored as hypotheses, and move the grid only on sustained evidence, bumping gridEpoch.
approach: Slice 1 (AC6): add a synthetic 3:2 polyrhythm ground-truth spec that pins today's beat level and tempo. No tracker change.

Slice 2: PhaseBank class with fixed Float32Arrays (PHASE_BINS=24 per beat, K=3 candidates). Each frame adds kick-weighted onset into bin (t - lastBeatTime) / period (O(1), no allocation). Each declared beat decays the bins by PHASE_DECAY and extracts the top K local maxima by scanning the bins.

Incumbent = the current grid phase (bin 0 after align). A challenger replaces it only if its score exceeds the incumbent's by PHASE_SWITCH_RATIO for PHASE_SWITCH_BEATS consecutive beats. This removes the need to wait for 8 silent beats.

On a switch, shift lastBeatTime by the challenger offset (bounded to under half a period), increment gridEpoch once, and never decrement beatCount. Optionally slew over 2 beats, but epoch still bumps exactly once.
rhythmAnalyzer passes the kick-band flux next to the summed onset. The kick weight is a new constant, so ONSET_BAND_WEIGHTS and halving/meter stay untouched.
Judge on scorecard, scorecard:check, sweep:gate and a CPU bench against main. Tune only the new PHASE_* constants. Remove it.fails markers that start passing.

Later separable slices, each shipped or reverted on its own: beat-presence gate using peak-to-mean of the bank (beatless, AC7), 3/2 rule (AC8), 6-8 and half-time level. Record before and after for every cell (AC9).

options.summary: Stop treating phase as something the PLL must track onset by onset; every beat, score all phases against the last ~12 beats of onset history with a comb, and move the grid when a rival phase clearly wins, leaving the PLL as the fine tracker.
approach: Break the assumption that phase is a local correction: it is a global estimate over recent history at the already-correct tempo, so dense onsets cannot hide a wrong lock.

Add PhaseComb in a new phaseComb.ts: 16 phase bins across one period, scored over the last 12 beats of the existing per-frame onset history (the 6 s the tracker already scans in declareBeat), with a +/-1 frame tolerance and recency weights.
Evidence is a sum of the full onset plus an extra low-band term (kick weight) used only inside the comb, so ONSET_BAND_WEIGHTS, halving and meter are untouched.
Call it from declareBeat each beat. Jump only if the best bin beats the current phase's score by a margin (about 1.25x) on 2 consecutive beats, so a single syncopated kick cannot capture the loop.
On a jump, reuse the changeOctave grid-move path: gridEpoch++, beatCount keeps counting, lastBeatTime and periodSeconds are set from the new grid. The PLL continues for fine tracking.
Retire the 8-lost-beats re-search as the only recovery path; keep it as a fallback.

Stretch, each separable: comb contrast (peak over mean) as a beat-presence score for beatless; the same comb over bar lengths (2, 3, 4 beats) for 6-8 and half-time beat level. 3/2 stays behind the AC6 grid spec.

options.summary: Measure first, then add a stateless phase comb (from O3) over the onset history BeatTracker already keeps, with O2's incumbent-versus-challenger hysteresis and a kick term used only inside the comb. A config switch reproduces today's tracker exactly, so every step is ablatable and revertible. The stretch slices reuse the comb's contrast (beat presence) and bar-length scoring (6-8, half-time), and 3/2 comes after the polyrhythm spec.
approach: S1 tooling: turn the summer2000 scratch script into a beat-error trace tool (per-beat error over time through detectFromPcm with loadWithOverrides), and add an offline tracker CPU bench that times RhythmAnalyzer and BeatTracker per frame against main

design.overview: Diagnose first, then make two separate small fixes, then do the stretch work. S1 adds a beat trace that prints, per beat: error against the taps; the phase check's bins, best place, ratio, phaseWins and phaseBeats (with each reset); the correction's chosen peak; the period; phaseShiftCount; and the gate's open time. It also adds an interleaved CPU bench, and records the summer2000 block, the latest first-move time that still allows AC1, and the fixed, ordered constant grid for S3. S2 pins a 3:2 polyrhythm grid. After S1, it adds the 16-seed noise and eighths harness with a kick-stream model, plus synthetics that reproduce the traced block (shown failing on main before it.fails is committed). S3 fixes summer2000 inside the existing checkPhase. Either it adds kick evidence (the peak-normalized band-0 term, on top of its existing onset weight), or it changes the winning-streak gate, whichever S1 shows is the block. S4 attempts low-bpm-rnb's slide, only if S1's trace shows the rival evidence stays on the taps through the slide window. The rival is folded relative to an anchor: the grid's phase at the last phase move or octave change, with the period held at the anchor. It clears when the period estimate moves more than BEAT_RIVAL_PERIOD_TOLERANCE (1 percent), and on octave and boundary changes. While a sustained rival disagrees with the grid, the correction may not pull the grid away from it, and the period follow is damped. S4 merges only if AC2 passes (D8). No phase move bumps gridEpoch (D10). S5 closes the required cells. S6 to S8 are stretch.

findings.finding: S4's core mechanism is not well-defined. The rival accumulator is 'folded on absolute time modulo the tempo period'. tempoPeriod comes from tempo.update() and is re-set through beat.setTempo() on every tempo update (rhythmAnalyzer.ts:156-160). The phase of a fixed absolute time t under modulo T moves by about t*dT/T^2, so at t=60 s and a 0.5 percent period change the whole fold shifts by about 0.4 beat, and the bins mean nothing across any estimate change. Only an octave or a large reinit is a 'tempo change' in AC10, so small drifts would silently corrupt the rival, or force a clear on every update, which removes the memory the veto needs. A fold relative to a fixed anchor time and a held period is a different design that the plan does not specify. On low-bpm-rnb the lock itself is a 162 to 81 halving, and changeOctave (beatTracker.ts:155-166) clears the bins right then, so the rival starts empty exactly when the grid is placed on the beat. The rival's evidence is also the same onset sum that the doc says band weights, window and gains could not separate. K2 rates the miss as high likelihood, so the design as written is likely to be a bounded miss.
findings.suggestion: Before S4 starts, require S1's low-bpm-rnb trace to show that the rival evidence (with the intended anchor and period handling) stays on the tap through the slide window. Write down the anchor (for example the grid's phase at the moment of the phase move, with the period held until the rival clears) and what resets it, and add a spec for a period estimate that moves 1 percent.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. The S4 rival is anchored on the grid's phase at the last move or octave change, with the period held. It clears on a period move above BEAT_RIVAL_PERIOD_TOLERANCE (1 percent) and on octave or boundary changes, and AC10 has a 1 percent period-move spec. S4 starts only if S1's trace shows the anchored rival stays on the taps through the slide window. It is otherwise a recorded miss under D8.

findings.finding: AC3 and the goals say gate.secondsAfterLock must not get worse on any track, while D9 says the gate is reported and not required. In scripts/scorecard/targets.ts:152-163 the cell is blocking:true with floor 4. scorecard:check only fails a blocking pass-to-fail change, so 'not worse' is not enforced for the tracks already failing (summer2000 at 6.1 s, half-time-shuffle 7.2, lonley 10.8) or for a passing track that gets slower but stays under 4 s. Conversely, a phase move after the dancer's lock makes the gate relearn its place on the tracker's beat, so the cell may well get worse on summer2000, and the plan then blocks S3 on a cell the tracker does not own. The two statements cannot both be gates.
findings.suggestion: State in AC3 how 'not worse' is checked (a numeric diff of every gate.secondsAfterLock cell against the baseline JSON, in the PR). Say what happens if summer2000's gate seconds rise while beat error falls: for example, it is accepted and reported with the trace's gate open time, as D9 implies.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. AC3 now requires a numeric diff of every gate cell against the baseline. Passing tracks may not go from pass to fail or rise by more than 0.5 s. A rise on tracks already failing is accepted and reported with the trace's gate open time (D9).

findings.finding: K1's guard is weaker than stated. The 'pre-registered grid, first point meeting AC1 with AC3 and AC10 green' selects on summer2000 itself. The held-out tracks are tracks that already pass, which can only show no regression, not that the constants generalise. A 'first point' rule also depends on the order of the grid, which is not fixed. The failure mode is that the kick weight is tuned until summer2000 clears 40 ms, with no check on any other failing or syncopated track (syncopation-no-kick, 6-8-time, syncopationbass, high-bpm-dnb first lock).
findings.suggestion: Fix the grid and its order in S1's output before running S3. Require that the chosen point does not move the non-target failing tracks' beat error or first lock worse than main. Report the whole grid's results in the PR, not only the chosen point.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. S1 fixes the grid and its order before S3. AC3 now requires the named weak tracks (syncopation-no-kick, 6-8-time, syncopationbass, high-bpm-dnb) no worse than main, and the whole grid goes in the PR (K1).

findings.finding: AC10's noise and eighths bounds (63 and 15) can pass vacuously and have no harness. The existing phase specs in app/features/rhythm/beatTracker.test.ts drive the envelope only, through push(time, onset), and the 16-seed noise figures are quoted in a comment at beatTracker.ts:28-31, not in a spec (no seed loop exists in beatTracker.test.ts). C2 says a missing kick counts as 0 and gives output identical to main, so a noise or eighths synthetic that does not feed a kick stream cannot show any difference from the S3 change. The bound has to be measured with a kick stream that is correlated with the noise and the eighths the way real low-band flux is, and the plan does not say how that stream is built. AC10's 'moves within 8 beats of reaching PHASE_MIN_BEATS' is also ill-defined (see F14).
findings.suggestion: S2 should add the 16-seed harness, with a stated kick-stream model (for example the low-band share of each synthetic onset, plus a version with kick-only noise), and record main's counts under that harness. Make the S3 bound apply to the kick-fed runs.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. S2 adds the 16-seed harness with a stated kick-stream model and records main's counts under it. AC10's bounds apply to the kick-fed runs.

findings.finding: S2's it.fails synthetic for a wrong first phase on a dense track will likely pass on main, which makes vitest fail the it.fails. beatTracker.test.ts:396-412 and 425-436 show that checkPhase already moves an off-beat start with envelope-only drive. Reproducing summer2000 needs the mechanism that blocks the check on real audio, and S1 has not found it yet. S2 has no depends_on S1, so the synthetic is written before the cause is known. The AC10 latency claim on that synthetic is only as good as its likeness to the real block.
findings.suggestion: Make S2 depend on S1 for the wrong-first-phase and early-kick synthetics (the 3:2 pin can stay independent). Build each synthetic to reproduce the trace's mechanism, and show that it fails on main before it.fails is committed.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. S2 now depends on S1. Its synthetics reproduce the traced mechanism and are shown failing on main before it.fails is committed.

findings.finding: In checkPhase (beatTracker.ts:332-339) phaseBeats is reset to 0 on any beat where the rival does not win, the same as phaseWins. So PHASE_MIN_BEATS (8) is really a run of 8 consecutive winning beats, not 'beats of evidence' as the comment and AC10 say. On a dense track a single beat where the grid's own 3-bin window ties or wins restarts the count, which is a possible reason for the silence on summer2000 that the plan does not list. It also makes AC10's 'within 8 beats of reaching PHASE_MIN_BEATS' ambiguous, and 'loosening PHASE_MIN_BEATS' in S3 changes a streak length, not an evidence minimum. With a 20-beat memory and a median over the post-lock beats, AC1 also needs the move early (the doc's diagnosis ends near 30 s), so the move latency on the real track matters, not only on the synthetic.
findings.suggestion: Have S1's trace print phaseBeats and phaseWins per beat, and the beat of each reset, and state the first-move beat on summer2000. Reword AC10 in terms of the winning streak. Add the latest first-move time that still allows AC1 as a number in S3.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. The trace prints phaseWins and phaseBeats with each reset. AC10 is worded in terms of the winning streak. S1 records the latest first-move time on summer2000 that still allows AC1, and S3 must meet it.

findings.finding: C2 says the 'low-band flux' goes straight into the bins, but the onset it is added to is normalised: rhythmAnalyzer.ts:147-155 divides each band's flux by its own decaying peak, because raw flux is a per-bin mean and the kick band is narrow. A raw kick flux would put the kick weight on a different scale per track and per loudness, which makes BEAT_PHASE_KICK_WEIGHT a per-track tuning constant. The kick already contributes ONSET_BAND_WEIGHTS[0] times its normalised flux to the onset, so the extra term double-counts it. C2's signature gives no definition.
findings.suggestion: Define kick in C2 as the same peak-normalised band-0 term that is used in the onset (flux / fluxPeak[0]), and state that the weight is added on top of the existing weight. Add it to the specs.
findings.resolution: Changed the plan. C2 defines kick as the peak-normalized band-0 term (flux[0] / fluxPeak[0]), with BEAT_PHASE_KICK_WEIGHT added on top of ONSET_BAND_WEIGHTS[0] in the phase bins only.

findings.finding: S5 depends_on S3 and S4, and S5 holds the AC9 documentation and the baseline rewrite for the required cells. S4 is expected to miss (K2 high likelihood, D8 says drop the branch), so the chain stops at a slice that is not merged. S6 to S8 depend only on S3, so they can ship before S5 closes, and each then rewrites the baseline or records cells without a closing slice.

findings.finding: S6 uses the phase evidence's peak over mean as the presence floor. That evidence (phaseBins) is only filled after BeatTracker is aligned (beatTracker.ts:190-194), so it cannot gate the first lock without moving the check ahead of align(). If beatlessNeverLocks measures the tempo lock, the bins do not exist at all there. Q3 and the S6 text allow tempo.ts but still name the phase evidence as the signal.
findings.suggestion: Keep S6 stretch, but say in S6 that the signal must come from a source that exists before the lock (tempo.ts autocorrelation contrast, or an align-time sum), decided after Q3.

freeze_first.name: tracker.state beat contract
freeze_first.definition: lastBeatTime, periodSeconds, beatCount and gridEpoch keep today's meaning. A phase move (checkPhase today, or the S4 veto) never bumps gridEpoch and increments phaseShiftCount. beatCount never decreases. Only a numbering break (a realign after lost beats, or a song change) bumps gridEpoch, as today. Hub, dancer gate, cubes and meter need no change, and the existing beatTracker.test.ts epoch specs pass unchanged.

freeze_first.name: BeatTracker.push signature
freeze_first.definition: push(time: number, onset: number, kick?: number): boolean. kick is the same peak-normalized band-0 term RhythmAnalyzer already uses in the onset (flux[0] / fluxPeak[0], rhythmAnalyzer.ts:147-155). BEAT_PHASE_KICK_WEIGHT is added on top of ONSET_BAND_WEIGHTS[0], in the phase bins only. When kick is omitted it counts as 0 and the result is identical to main. There is no new history ring: kick is folded per frame into the O(PHASE_BINS) bins and, in S4, the rival accumulator.
